chapter: South America and back in New York
title: Zurich and an abortive trip to the Matterhorn
summary: On the way to Spain they play Zurich and take a taxi toward the Matterhorn, which proves far farther than it looks.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: So, there are a lot of firsts there. And where we left it, you had just returned to New York from South America, but I understand we left -- we skipped a few things and I think we should go back to, I think, 1925, and you tell us what we skipped. When you went to Spain the first time.

Well, I'll tell you, we had a wonderful time. On our way to Spain. We broke the jump in Switzerland. And, it was a funny thing. The reason why I'm thinking of this Chris, is because we were playing in Zurich. And right out of Zurich is one of those tremendous peaks that Switzerland is known for. I think it was the Matterhorn. Yeah, it was the Matterhorn, see. So, as we -- so, one afternoon a couple of

boys and I said we'll take a ride up to this mountain and then we'd be back for the evening show. Well, before we could get back for the evening show, we never got to the mountain. Because, to us, it looked like it was about 15 or 10 miles away, and we hired a taxicab and we was going to ride up there and ride back. But, evidently, it must have been about 40 miles away, but that's the way it looked to us. So, anyhow, we got back. When we got back, we was glad to get back in and be ready for the show. Because we missed supper and everything, because we'd gone so far. Because we didn't realize. Because being from New York, we didn't know that there would be such a long ways away to look at a mountain peak that looks like it's ten miles away when it's forty miles away.
